For any other read failure, such as an I/O error, every session exits at startup with a message to contact an administrator.

rules.reason: The dashboard can't read {file}, so it can't tell which values that file sets. It can't tell whether Claude Code reads it either. To check, run /status in a new session started in this project. Its Setting sources line lists each settings file Claude Code loaded.

{file} isn't valid JSON, or its top level isn't an object, so the dashboard can't tell what it sets. Claude Code refuses to start while a managed file is in that state, so no new session starts until it's fixed. To check, start claude in a terminal. The error it prints names the file.

quotes.quote: When a managed settings file, drop-in file, MDM plist, or HKLM registry value is present but can't be parsed as a JSON object, Claude Code refuses to start and prints an error naming the source, even when another admin source delivers a valid policy.

rules.reason: {file} isn't valid JSON, or its top level isn't an object. Claude Code skips the whole file, so nothing in it applies. The next file or Claude Code's default decides each value instead. To see what's wrong, run claude doctor in a terminal.
{file} is in the {layer} rules folder, and Claude Code loads only .md files there. User and project rules both load, user rules first, and neither overrides the other.

quotes.quote: Claude Code loads user-level rules before project rules, so a project rule appears later in Claude's context than a user rule. Neither set overrides the other: if a user rule and a project rule conflict, Claude may follow either one, so keep the two consistent.
